instruments.title: MiFID II Article 16(6) — Record-keeping by investment firms
instruments.status_note: Status taken from the Official Journal text; the consolidated version was not compared, because EUR-Lex refuses automated retrieval.
instruments.applies_to: Investment firms authorised under MiFID II
instruments.summary: Article 16(6) requires records sufficient for supervision but states no retention period. The periods come from Article 16(7) for recorded communications and MiFIR Article 25(1) for order and transaction data. Commission Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Article 72 sets the storage-medium conditions.

obligations.title: Storage medium must reveal every correction and prevent manipulation
obligations.applies_to: Investment firms
obligations.requirement: Keep records on a medium that the authority can readily access to reconstitute each key stage of a transaction, where corrections and the prior contents are easily ascertainable, and which cannot otherwise be manipulated or altered.

source.quote: (a) the competent authority is able to access them readily and to reconstitute each key stage of the processing of each transaction; (b) it is possible for any corrections or other amendments, and the contents of the records prior to such corrections or amendments, to be easily ascertained; (c) it is not possible for the records otherwise to be manipulated or altered;
source.text_as_of: OJ L 87, 31.3.2017 (original text)

obligations.title: Order and transaction data kept five years
obligations.applies_to: Investment firms
obligations.requirement: Keep the relevant data on every order and transaction in financial instruments, whether on own account or for a client, at the competent authority's disposal for five years.

retention.trigger: The Article states the period without naming its start.

source.quote: 1. Investment firms shall keep at the disposal of the competent authority, for five years, the relevant data relating to all orders and all transactions in financial instruments which they have carried out, whether on own account or on behalf of a client.
source.text_as_of: OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text)

verified.by: claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel)
verified.method: Quote compared verbatim against the Official Journal text from publications.europa.eu. The consolidated version was not compared.

obligations.title: Recorded calls and electronic communications kept five years, up to seven on request
obligations.applies_to: Investment firms dealing on own account or providing client order services
obligations.requirement: Keep recordings of relevant telephone conversations and electronic communications for five years, or up to seven years where the competent authority requests it, and provide them to the client on request.

retention.trigger: The Article states the period without naming its start.

source.quote: The records kept in accordance with this paragraph shall be provided to the client involved upon request and shall be kept for a period of five years and, where requested by the competent authority, for a period of up to seven years.
source.text_as_of: OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text)

verified.by: claude-opus-5 agent session (not reviewed by counsel)
verified.method: Quote compared verbatim against the Official Journal text from publications.europa.eu. The consolidated version was not compared.

obligations.title: Keep records of all services, activities and transactions sufficient for supervision
obligations.applies_to: Investment firms
obligations.requirement: Keep records of every service, activity and transaction that are sufficient for the competent authority to supervise, enforce, and confirm compliance with obligations to clients and to market integrity. The Article itself sets no retention period.
obligations.note: Article 16(6) has no duration. The periods that apply to these records come from Article 16(7) for communications and MiFIR Article 25(1) for orders and transactions.

source.quote: 6. An investment firm shall arrange for records to be kept of all services, activities and transactions undertaken by it which shall be sufficient to enable the competent authority to fulfil its supervisory tasks and to perform the enforcement actions under this Directive, Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, Directive 2014/57/EU and Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, and in particular to ascertain that the investment firm has complied with all obligations including those with respect to clients or potential clients and to the integrity of the market.
source.text_as_of: OJ L 173, 12.6.2014 (original text)

obligations.title: Swap records kept five years after the transaction ends
obligations.applies_to: CFTC records entities holding records of swaps or related cash or forward transactions
obligations.requirement: Keep regulatory records of each swap or related cash or forward transaction from creation until the transaction terminates, matures, expires, or is transferred, assigned or novated, and for at least five years after that.

retention.trigger: Termination, maturity, expiration, transfer, assignment or novation date of the transaction

source.quote: (1) A records entity shall keep regulatory records of any swap or related cash or forward transaction (as defined in § 23.200(i) of this chapter), other than regulatory records required by § 23.202(a)(1) and (b)(1)-(3) of this chapter, from the date the regulatory record was created until the termination, maturity, expiration, transfer, assignment, or novation date of the transaction and for a period of not less than five years after such date.
source.text_as_of: eCFR, up to date as of 2026-09-16

obligations.title: Order memoranda with time of receipt, entry and execution

obligations.title: Do not destroy, alter or falsify records to obstruct a federal matter
obligations.applies_to: Any person
obligations.requirement: Do not knowingly destroy, alter, conceal or falsify any record with intent to obstruct a federal investigation or bankruptcy case, including one only contemplated. The penalty is imprisonment of up to 20 years. In practice this means suspending routine deletion under a legal hold once such a matter is reasonably anticipated.

source.quote: Whoever knowingly alters, destroys, mutilates, conceals, covers up, falsifies, or makes a false entry in any record, document, or tangible object with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States or any case filed under title 11, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter or case, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.

controls.title: Tamper-evident audit trail of record creation, modification and deletion
controls.implementation: Log S3 data events for every records bucket to a CloudTrail trail with log file integrity validation. Keep the trail in an Object Lock bucket in a separate log-archive account. Versioning on the records buckets keeps prior content, so a modified record can be re-created. This combination is what the 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(A) audit-trail alternative requires. Firms that choose the WORM option still need an input audit system under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and this trail provides it.
evidence: CloudTrail trail configuration with data events on the records buckets and LogFileValidationEnabled true
Periodic output of validate-logs showing the digest chain intact
Log-archive bucket Object Lock configuration
controls.limits: CloudTrail records API actions, not business-level edits made inside an application database. An application that changes records before writing them to S3 needs its own audit trail.

aws.service: AWS CloudTrail (data events, log file integrity validation)
aws.configuration: Organization trail, S3 data events for records buckets, log file validation on, delivered to a locked log-archive bucket
Event data store for queryable retention of the same events

controls.title: Capture and retain business communications and recorded calls
controls.implementation: Route every approved business communication channel (email, chat, recorded telephony) to capture that writes into the WORM records buckets under the communications retention class. For telephony on Amazon Connect, send call recordings to a locked bucket. Channels that cannot be captured are prohibited for business use, mirroring the Article 16(7) duty to prevent unrecordable communications on private equipment.
evidence: Channel inventory showing the capture path for each approved channel
Connect instance storage configuration pointing recordings at the locked bucket
Surveillance sampling reports that confirm capture completeness
controls.limits: Capturing third-party messaging apps needs vendor archiving connectors, which are outside this corpus.

aws.configuration: Recordings delivered to an Object Lock bucket under the communications retention class

controls.title: Legal holds for indefinite retention and anticipated investigations
controls.implementation: Place an Object Lock legal hold on life-of-enterprise records (charter documents, minute books, registration forms), because a legal hold has no expiry date. Keep a documented legal-hold procedure. When a federal investigation or proceeding is reasonably anticipated, it places holds on the relevant records and suspends lifecycle expiration for them, so routine deletion cannot become the destruction that 18 U.S.C. 1519 criminalises.
evidence: Legal-hold register listing each matter, its scope, the date the hold was placed, and who authorised it
S3 object metadata showing ObjectLockLegalHoldStatus ON for held objects
CloudTrail events for PutObjectLegalHold, showing who placed and removed each hold
controls.limits: The technical hold only works if the procedure is triggered in time. Knowing when a matter is contemplated is a legal judgement, not something the platform decides.

aws.configuration: Legal hold ON for life-of-enterprise classes and for records in scope of an active matter

controls.title: Separately stored, locked redundant copy
controls.implementation: Back up the records buckets with AWS Backup to a vault in a separate AWS account, with Vault Lock in compliance mode and a minimum retention of at least the longest period in the retention schedule. Keep the copy in the project's designated region unless a second region has been deliberately approved. The separation that matters here is account and credential isolation, which protects against the loss of the primary system.

Restore-test records proving the copy can serve as the redundant set

controls.title: Executive and third-party undertakings for electronic records
controls.implementation: File the 17a-4(f)(3)(v) undertaking with the designated examining authority, signed by a designated executive officer (who may appoint designated officers and specialists) or by a designated third party. For records held in a cloud provider's storage, either obtain the provider's full 17a-4(i)(1)(i) undertaking, or establish and document independent access. Independent access means the firm can reach, examine and furnish the records without the provider's intervention, which makes the shorter 17a-4(i)(1)(ii) undertaking available.
evidence: Filed undertakings, with the date and recipient of each filing
Written appointments of designated officers and specialists
An independent-access test showing the firm retrieving and producing records using only its own credentials
controls.limits: No AWS configuration satisfies this control. It is a filing and a governance act that the firm must perform.

controls.title: Retention schedule mapping record classes to periods and triggers
controls.implementation: Keep a retention schedule, generated from this corpus's export, that assigns every record class a period, a trigger and an accessibility window. Put fixed-from-creation classes in buckets whose default retention equals the period. Trigger-based classes (account closure, end of fiscal year, transaction termination, end of the enterprise) cannot know their end date at write time. Write them with the minimum known retention, then extend the retain-until date when the trigger event occurs. Compliance mode allows extending a retention period but never shortening it. Where regimes overlap, take the longest applicable period.
evidence: The retention schedule, versioned, with each row citing an obligation id from this corpus
S3 Inventory reports showing each object's retain-until date against the schedule
Records of the jobs that extend retention on trigger events, for example S3 Batch Operations manifests and completion reports
controls.limits: The corpus carries the regulatory floor only. Litigation, tax and client-contract retention can exceed it and must be added to the schedule separately.

controls.title: Non-rewriteable, non-erasable record storage
controls.implementation: Write regulatory records only to S3 buckets created with Object Lock enabled and a default retention in compliance mode. Compliance mode is the WORM option in Rule 17a-4(f)(2)(i)(B). Governance mode is not, because privileged users can bypass it. Enable versioning (Object Lock requires it) so that a correction is written as a new version and the prior content survives, which is what Delegated Regulation 2017/565 Article 72(1)(b) asks for.
evidence: Bucket ObjectLockConfiguration showing ObjectLockEnabled and a DefaultRetention in COMPLIANCE mode
AWS Config rule s3-bucket-default-lock-enabled reporting COMPLIANT for every records bucket
The Cohasset Associates compliance assessment of S3 Object Lock that AWS links from its documentation, filed with the control evidence
controls.limits: The Cohasset assessment covers the storage layer only. The firm still owns the retention schedule, the audit system for inputs under 17a-4(f)(3)(iii), and the undertakings.
